boundary_note: Replacement boundaries require phase-level chronology and review; date-only source summaries are insufficient. No claims are admitted to enriched modeling.

claims.value: NPS lists US 65,085 and Confederate 44,968 as forces engaged; these are not verified opening strength.
claims.rationale: Whole-engagement totals may include reinforcements; do not condition opening expectations on later arrivals.

claims.value: NPS attributes the absence of fortification to Grant.
claims.rationale: A candidate mediator if replacement precedes preparation; source interpretation still requires review.

citations.quote: Grant did not choose to fortify his position; rather, he set about drilling his men many of which were raw recruits.

claims.value: Grant was ordered to await Buell at Pittsburg Landing.
claims.rationale: Orders from a superior constrain his choices, but need the original order and its timing.

citations.quote: Grant received orders to await Buell's Army of the Ohio at Pittsburg Landing.

claims.value: Beauregard took over after Johnston was mortally wounded.
claims.rationale: A single lead commander cannot receive the entire two-day residual without attribution review.

citations.quote: Johnston had been mortally wounded earlier and his second in command, Gen. P.G.T. Beauregard, took over.

claims.value: NPS says Beauregard did not know Buell's army had arrived.
claims.rationale: A retrospective statement about knowledge needs corroboration; do not infer the same information for all phases.

citations.quote: Beauregard was unaware of the arrival of Buell's army

claims.rationale: Source outcome is distinct from campaign contribution.
Not established by the sources inspected for this draft.

open_questions: Establish separate April 6 and April 7 force availability and command intervals.
Locate the original order to await Buell and contemporary accounts of Confederate intelligence.
Compare NPS figures to independently authored scholarship; duplicate NPS summaries are not independent confirmation.
